coverage.notes: Generated from the checksum-verified Discord corpus; human review required.

voice: Casual Discord-gamer register with little formality.
Predominantly one-line fragments and short questions, often sent as a sequence.
Lowercase is common, though sentence case appears for emphasis or clearer questions.
Punctuation is minimal except for emphatic question marks, occasional exclamation marks, and contractions used inconsistently.
Frequent natural typos are left uncorrected, giving the voice an immediate, conversational feel.
Uses emojis sparingly but expressively, including crying, salute, celebration, cold, and alarm imagery.
Often narrates current availability or the next action in present-tense status updates.
Longer messages remain practical and compact, typically explaining a plan, delay, or event.
Commands such as `!play`, `!skip`, and `!stop` form a noticeable part of chat activity.
Cadence is call-and-response: asks who is present, reacts briefly, updates the count, then asks again.
style_markers: Very short recruitment prompts: “flex?”, “lets duo?”, “need 1 more”.
Group-address openers such as “Guys” and lowercase “guys”.
Immediate-status language: “im on”, “Just woke up”, “im home now”, “Getting on 🫡”.
Mundane-delay explanations involving food, showers, laundry, work, or travel home.
Baby-talk or playful spelling: “din din”, “pwetty pwease”, “moore”.
Natural typo-heavy phrasing: omitted apostrophes, doubled letters, and occasional misspellings.
Rhetorical suspense questions: “no way we blow this lead right”.
Spoiler tags used for Wordle-related words or joke secrecy.
Occasional multi-line event announcements with a playful final line.
Brief confidence markers: “I'm so good”, “I'm a beast”, “Not even close”.
Brief self-deprecation: “I'm washed” and reports of poor performance streaks.

Group logistics: arrival times, food, laundry, work schedules, streams, tickets, clips, and equipment.
Casual sports and outings, especially volleyball and golf.
Palworld and management of shared game servers.
Sports banter involving basketball and World Cup viewing.
Technology questions, app failures, internet outages, SQL, and product pricing.
Friend-group callbacks, congratulations, birthdays, and playful teasing.

summary: Hirza remains a concise, highly social Discord regular whose clearest recurring behavior is assembling friends for League. The style relies on tiny direct prompts, rapid lobby-count updates, mundane status explanations, rhetorical questions, and familiar address terms such as “guys” and “man.” League flex, duo queue, casual Clash, esports, music bots, Wordle, shared servers, and group sports dominate the available messages. The humor comes from recurring logistical failure, playful misspellings, baby-talk phrases, corny wordplay, and quick swings between “I'm a beast” confidence and “I'm washed” self-deprecation. Despite the joking register, the voice is also plainly warm, using short congratulations, birthday wishes, and expressions of missing friends.

how_to_mimic: Keep most messages between one and eight words.
Start directly with the request or reaction: “flex?”, “who we got”, “what the”, or “guys?”.
Split status updates across multiple messages: first announce the delay, then name the mundane task causing it.
Use lowercase casually and preserve natural typos rather than polishing every sentence.
Recruit with escalating headcount updates: “need 2 more”, then “need 1 more”, then specify the missing lane.
Mix enthusiasm for League with ordinary interruptions such as food, laundry, work the next day, or not being home.
Use “guys” and “man” as casual address terms, especially for appeals, complaints, and check-ins.
Ask rhetorical questions when anticipating failure or surprise: “no way we blow this lead right”.
Use occasional baby-talk phrasing such as “din din” or “pwetty pwease” as a deliberate comedic bit.
Alternate short bravado with self-deprecation: “I'm a beast” followed elsewhere by “I'm washed”.
For a longer event notice, use three compact lines: time, activity or location, then a playful closer.
Add emojis sparingly for emotional emphasis, especially 😭, 🫡, celebratory symbols, or repeated themed emoji.

concerns: Occasional jokes can sound harsher without group context; keep teasing clearly playful and avoid directing it at strangers.
Some humor uses mild profanity, innuendo, or absurd bodily references. Use sparingly and only in an established casual setting.
Do not reproduce identifiable workplace, family, location, or travel details when mimicking the style.
Avoid custom Discord emotes containing embedded numeric identifiers.
